title: How I Finally Fixed My Screen-Time Habit
script: Narrator: [honestly] Last year, my screen-time report said nine hours a day. Nine hours, just looking at my phone.
Narrator: [surprised] I did not believe it at first. I thought the app was broken, so I checked it again the next week.
Narrator: [thoughtful] It was not broken. I really was spending most of my free time scrolling, without even choosing to.
Narrator: [reflective] I would open one app to check the time, and forty minutes later, I was still there, watching random videos.
Narrator: [honestly] My sleep got worse too. I checked messages in bed, and then I could not fall asleep for an hour.
Narrator: [determined] So I decided to make small changes, nothing extreme, just small rules I could actually follow.
Narrator: [thoughtful] First, I moved my most-used apps off my home screen, into a folder on the second page.
Narrator: [gently] That tiny change made a real difference. I stopped opening them without thinking, out of pure habit.
Narrator: [warmly] Second, I bought a cheap alarm clock, so my phone could finally stay outside my bedroom at night.
Narrator: [honestly] The first few nights felt strange, almost uncomfortable, like something important was missing from the room.
Narrator: [peacefully] But after about a week, I started falling asleep faster, and waking up without immediately reaching for my phone.
Narrator: [thoughtful] Third, I turned off most notifications, except messages from close family and a few important work apps.
Narrator: [warmly] My phone became quiet, and honestly, my mind became quieter too, in a way I had not expected.
Narrator: [reflective] I still use my phone every day, for work, for messages, for useful things. That has not changed.
Narrator: [gently] What changed is that I choose when to open it now, instead of it constantly pulling my attention away.
Narrator: [with a small smile] My screen-time report now says about three hours a day. I finally believe that number is real.
